misconceptions.description: Writing the design memo as a chronological summary of what was done instead of an argument for a recommended decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner narrates the steps taken across the module without stating a recommendation a reader must act on
misconceptions.feedback: A design memo argues, it does not recount. Lead with the recommendation and the decision it answers, then use the module work as supporting evidence.

misconceptions.description: Writing the memo with no named audience or decision owner, so it is unclear who must decide what
misconceptions.trigger: learner addresses the memo to no one and names no decision the reader is being asked to make
misconceptions.feedback: Name the audience and the decision they own. A memo to no one, about no decision, cannot be acted on.

misconceptions.description: Hiding the recommendation in the last paragraph so a busy reader cannot find what is being proposed
misconceptions.trigger: learner places the actual recommendation only at the end after several paragraphs of background
misconceptions.feedback: Put the recommendation up front (a BLUF, bottom line up front). Background supports the recommendation; it should not bury it.

misconceptions.description: Listing module evidence without tying each piece to the specific claim it supports in the recommendation
misconceptions.trigger: learner appends pilot data or audit results that are never connected to the recommended decision
misconceptions.feedback: Tie each evidence item to the claim it backs. Unlinked data is decoration; linked data is the argument.
